The Water Cycle

Water moves continuously between the ocean, atmosphere and land. Evaporation occurs when sunlight heats water in rivers, lakes and the sea. The water vapour rises and forms clouds. When clouds become heavy enough, water falls as rain or snow. This is called precipitation.

expectations.criterion: The adaptedContent is grammatically correct Afrikaans and accurately conveys the same information as the English source, including the water cycle stages.

rubric: Evaluate whether the Afrikaans text is fluent, grade-appropriate, and captures all scientific content from the source: evaporation, water vapour, clouds, precipitation.

South Africa's Biomes

South Africa has nine major biomes ranging from the Succulent Karoo, one of the world's biodiversity hotspots, to the vast Savanna that covers 33% of the country's land surface. The Fynbos biome, found mostly in the Western Cape, is home to over 9 000 plant species, 70% of which are endemic.

expectations.criterion: The Afrikaans text preserves all statistical data (nine biomes, 33%, 9 000 plant species, 70% endemic), SA place names (Wes-Kaap, Savanna, Fynbos, Suksulente Karoo), and does not fabricate any facts.

rubric: Verify: nine biomes, 33%, 9 000 plant species, 70% endemic, Western Cape reference. No invented statistics.
